newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-AUSTRALIAN SPORTS NEWS - AUGUST 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-AUSTRALIAN SPORTS NEWS - AUGUST 8.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australia's opening cricket batsmen Mark Taylor and Matthew Elliott placed the team in a favourable position in the fifth Ashes Test against England at Trent Bridge yesterday. Taylor, who won the toss for the fifth time in the series, elected to bat on what is the best wicket of the series. Page 20.

The Australian Football League Tribunal last night suspended Carlton's Luke O'Sullivan for four matches following an investigation by the Adelaide club on behalf of their player Trent Ormand-Allen. O'Sullivan was found guilty of breaking Ormand-Allen's aw in a match last Sunday, yet both players' evidence conflicted, and there was no video evidence. Page 20.

The New South Wales' rugby union team's hopes of re-signing Ben Kennedy have been lost after Kennedy said he knew nothing of negotiations to switch back to union from league. Kennedy is currently playing for the Canberra Raiders Super League team, and is contracted until 1999. Page 18.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The Sydney Swans Australian Football League team are expecting another full house for their match against St Kilda at the Sydney Cricket Ground on Sunday. However, the Swans will be without Tony Lockett and defender Dale Lewis, who are both out on suspenions. Page 47.

It is believed the main elements of a plan for rugby league peace, which was approved by key figures involved in both the Australian Rugby League and Super League, would be the naming of the competition as Super League, and the appointment of a chief exective to be made by News Limited. Page 48.

Former Australian rugby union great Stan Pilecki says the only obstacle the Wallabies face against the New Zealand All Blacks, who they play next weekend in Dunedin, is their lack of confidence. Pilecki said that while the All Blacks will be hard to beat, they are beatable. Page 48.
THE AGE
Australian athlete Melinda Gainsford-Taylor looks set to win a medal in the 200 metres at the world athletics championship in Athens after running the fastest time of the second round last night.
Gainsford-Taylor, who now moves into the semi-finals, won her heat in 22.45 seconds. Page D2.

Australian high-jumper Tim Forsyth admitted yesterday he was provoked by the arrogance of Javier Sotomayor of Cuba, who took the gold in the event at the world athletics champtionships in Athens, with Forsyth taking the bronze. Sotomayor waved a Cuban flag as he walked across the front of the pit as Forsyth stood at the top preparing to jump. Page D2.

The Australian under-23 basketball team will meet the United States in the quarter-finals of the under-23 world championships in Melbourne, yet the confrontation is taking place earlier than the Australians expected. Coach Ian Stacker said his team had hoped to meet the US in the gold medal play-offs, but because of an early loss to Turkey the team did not get the draw they had counted on. Page D11.
THE HERALD SUN

For the second week in a row, the Western Bulldogs Australian Football League team axed five senior players from its line-up following the team's fourth consecutive loss. Football manager Garry O'Sullivan said the players had to pay the price for the tea's poor form. Page 110.

Young Brisbane Australian Football Leauge players Daniel Bradshaw and Justin Leppitsch combined last week to kick 11 goals in the game against Hawthorn, and are hoping for similar form in tonight's game against North Melbourne at the Melbourne Cricket Grond. Page 104.

Victorian Racing Industry betting services general manager Stephen Allinson yesterday announced a number of new betting initiatives that will see the interstate betting rings merged, and more bookmakers using computers. Page 100.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

American boxing promoter Bob Arum says Australian boxer Kostya Tszyu will never be given the chance to fight Vince Phillips or Oscar de la Hoya after Tszyu's promoter Vlad Warton decided to take on a fight for Troy Waters which will be staged by Arum's arch rival Don King. Page 126.

As the prospect of peace in rugby league draws closer, television stations are looking to carve up the finishing product. It is expected if the proposed 14-team competition goes ahead, all seven club competition matches each week will be shown live on television, but this will be divided up between free-to-air and pay-TV companies. Page 123.

The Sydney Sandpipers netball coach Margaret Corbett has concerns for her team in the Commonwealth Bank Trophy, with her captain Sue Kenny now joining Carissa Tombs on the bench with an injury. The loss of Kenny, a key play maker, will hit the team hard. Page 117.
